newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Russian delegation in Bulgaria for talks.
newsitem.headline: Russian delegation in Bulgaria for talks.

text.p: A Russian delegation headed by Deputy Prime Minister Oleg Lobov started talks with Bulgaria's interim government on Monday on boosting economic relations between the two countries, officials said.
Russia's delegation includes Gazprom president Rem Vyahirev, representatives of the central bank, atomic industry and national carrier Aeroflot.

Equipment supplies for the reconstruction of Bulgaria's Soviet-made nuclear power plant at Kozloduy, a gas pipeline project and air transport cooperation will be among the issues to be discussed, Lobov said on arrival on Monday.
"The Kozloduy equipment can be supplied against a $50 million Russian debt to Bulgaria," Lobov told reporters, adding that a credit could also be considered.
Bulgaria, which plans to become a distribution centre for Russian natural gas in the Balkans, last month invited bidders for two pipeline concessions for transiting Russian gas through its territory.

The Bulgarian-Russian joint stock company Topenergy, which was set up in 1995, is considered as a serious candidate for the concessions. Gazprom has 50 percent in Topenergy and Bulgargas holds a 25.1 percent stake. The remaining 24.9 percent is distributed among Bulgarian banks and firms.
